chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Fletcher at the piano before dawn
summary: Fletcher often fumbled at the piano at 5 or 6 am, thinking up charts, sometimes interrupted by Benny Goodman's calls; Horace too likes to write early.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did he like to -- at times when he wasn't on the job or just, say, in his apartment or something, did he like to just, from time to time sit at the piano and goof around?

Yes. Yes. Even Early in the morning, about 5:00 or 6:00 o'clock, sometimes he would be downstairs, and his wife would be upstairs sleeping. Sometimes when I was there, I'd be there the same way and I'd listen, hear (unintelligible) playing the piano downstairs, and he'd be down just fumbling around and thinking of -- and playing pretty chords, you know, and he got so he'd like to do this because a lot of times Benny used to interrupt

him anyway, Benny Goodman. (He) would call him up at that hour of the morning, and it just got so that it was hard for him to get to sleep. And sometimes he'd get to sleep. He said he'd wake up. He had an idea, and he'd come down to the piano and fool around and play it. Then he'd jot it down. He'd go back to back to bed. See? And as you know, sometimes early in the morning the best arrangements are written. Everything was real nice and quiet around, you know; you'd hear a bird or two every now and then outside, you know, and everything else is quiet. So this is the time that I really like to work best.
